reviews.review:
this game is great. of the many times i played it i have had many different experiences. i won't speak of online because i don't really have much time in it and haven't tried lately to see if it is still thriving.
i am not huge on 40K so i can't really say a lot, but i do enjoy their action oriented games.

the story of this game is that a planet with an invictus robot, a giant mech, is being attacked and you are ordered to protect the planet because that factory and mech are incredibly important. you fend off the orks as you protect your soldiers and sabotage them to get the upper hand while trying to get to the mech. half way through you meet an inquisitor who is trying to protect his secret research which can wipe out the orks on the planet. in doing so you cause a warp event and give the forces of chaos the chance to invade the planet and their leader to ascend using that object, which you go after alone since you are found out to have resistance to the warp, which isn't normal.

gameplay is very heavy feeling, you feel a little sluggish, and enemies can feel like they take more shots than they really should. like it feels like enemies are a bit too spongy. but i guess it makes sense, in 40K everything is pretty hard to kill normally. it is an interesting mix of shooter and hack and slasher. you get a very nice variety of weapons split into 3 different weapon slots. which as you get further through the game most of them end up being your secondary weapon which cuts down on how much mix and match you can do to have fun using them all. everything feels like it has impact even while feeling like you don't do enough damage, but nothing is incredibly hard, outside of some encounters meant to push you.

music is good, it has good power to it and helps you get into the moments when you get absorbed into it.

the game still looks fantastic, even after all this time. everything is so grand and enormous, and so cool to see. i personally can go back and fourth of, 40K goes over the top, and it hits that sweet spot of BEING over the top. but overall, i had a lot of fun looking around this playthrough.

A little dated but still a fun short campaign. Its kinda like Gears of War meets God of War crossed with a bit of the gunplay of the first Uncharted minus the cover system. The system for dealing through fatality kills is a bit broken as it makes you super vulnerable to getting completely destroyed before the animation finishes. But other than that it plays alright. If you're into Warhammer 40k its worth a play.

Warning: This game has next to no Linux compatibility, even under Proton. I had to use a no-CD patch just to run it and a dinput library override to prevent it from crashing midway through. Don't expect a plug-and-play experience if your configuration is similar to mine.
Once I managed to make it run I could lock it at 144fps with my hardware barely noticing something was happening, tho.

Now, what to actually say about the game? It's fine. Nothing mindblowing here; get it on sale and it's good fun for the money. The story is serviceable, and the core gameplay loop is fun and has aged pretty well, despite feeling like it's straight from the Xbox 360 era.

There are a few caveats with some sections that aged worse than others. Specifically, the level where you have to fight turrets instead of orks is quite bad, to be honest. Luckily, the turrets can be easily killed by shooting them through cover, otherwise, they would be incredibly tedious to fight.

Other sections are awesome, though. The jetpack+hammer combo is the real highlight. Jumping through huge arenas filled with enemies and smashing them around... I don't know about you, but that's about as much as I can ask of any video game.

Even just moving around makes you feel heavy, and I mean that in the most positive way possible. Every weapon, both melee and ranged, is satisfying to use. Enemies respond well to your blows, and you generally feel like your character is actually wearing that huge power armor.

Game balance is a bit all over the place, though, with ranged enemies dealing way too much damage compared to melee ones. However, I completed the game in 8 hours using a Steam Controller (with gyro aim) on maximum difficulty, and I'd say my skills are quite average.

On that topic: the campaign doesn't overstay its welcome, but it is on the short side. You can surely squeeze more time out of it if you're a completionist, but I still highly suggest getting this game on sale.

The story itself is fine: a decent military fantasy with sci-fi chivalry undertones. This is my entry point into the Warhammer 40k franchise, so I didn't know exactly what to expect but, after watching an hour-long video on the lore, I can say it feels pretty accurate. Mind you, there's nothing groundbreaking happening here; the story is just there to make you smash some orks. That simplicity is actually a strength in my opinion, as nothing gets in the way of you wreaking havoc.

So, should you buy it? I don't think it's worth its full price tag, but it is a good game. If you're in the market for a solid military/power armor fantasy or you just want to play it before going to the sequel, go for it. Just avoid it if you're a Linux user unwilling to go the extra length to prevent it from silently crashing on boot.
